The driver, not a dispatcher

Meet Chong

Years spent showing visitors around Chiang Mai and the mountains north of it — elephant care mornings, sticky waterfalls barefoot, the long climb to the highest point in the country. Families with young kids, retired couples, groups who just wanted a good driver and someone who knew where to eat.

Every trip is Chong behind the wheel, in his own car — never a dispatched stranger, never a shared minivan. Fluent English throughout, a pace that's flexible, and a happy detour for khao soi that isn't in any guidebook.

English spoken No fixed itinerary One driver, start to finish LINE & WhatsApp friendly

Wachirathan Waterfall

Bua Tong Sticky Waterfall

KRIElephants

Krisdadoi Elephant Care

Feed, bathe, and stand forehead-to-trunk with the herd at an ethical, no-riding camp.

Get directions
AIMRange

Shooting Range Day

Supervised target practice with safety gear provided — a popular add-on for groups.

Get directions
CFECoffee

Mountain Coffee Stop

A coffee stop with a mountain view, somewhere between routes — good coffee, better view.

WRKTemple

Wat Rong Khun (White Temple), Chiang Rai

An intricately white temple, still being built by artist Chalermchai Kositpipat, with mirrored glass that catches the sun. About three hours from Chiang Mai — usually a full day or an overnight combined with other Chiang Rai stops.

Get directions
MRMCulture

Mae Rim Tea Garden & Long-Neck Karen Village

A terraced green tea garden just north of the city, a short walk from a Kayan (long-neck Karen) village where you can meet the community and see their handwoven textiles. About 45 minutes from the Old City.

Get directions
BLUTemple

Wat Rong Suea Ten (Blue Temple)

A striking all-blue temple in Chiang Rai, built by a student of the White Temple's artist. Often visited together with Wat Rong Khun and the Big Buddha as a full Chiang Rai temple day.

Get directions
BUDBig Buddha

Wat Huay Pla Kung

Home to a giant white Guanyin statue and a nine-tier pagoda you can climb for views over Chiang Rai — striking after dark when it's lit up.

Get directions
LTCCafe

Lalita Cafe

A cafe built into a landscaped waterfall garden — worth the stop for the setting as much as the coffee.

Get directions

The local calendar

Chiang Mai's festivals & traditions

Exact dates shift every year — many follow the lunar calendar. Ask your driver to check the current year's dates.

JANUmbrellas

Bo Sang Umbrella Festival

The hand-painted umbrella village east of the city holds a parade and craft fair, usually mid-January.

FEBFlowers

Chiang Mai Flower Festival

A flower-covered parade and garden displays at Suan Buak Hat park, timed to when the cool-season blooms peak, early February.

APRSongkran

Songkran Water Festival

Thai New Year, mid-April. Chiang Mai's celebration runs longer and louder than most — the moat becomes one long water fight.

MAYCity Pillar

Inthakin (City Pillar) Festival

An eight-day merit-making festival at Wat Chedi Luang, honoring the city's guardian pillar — usually May or June.

NOVLanterns

Yi Peng & Loy Krathong

On the November full moon, sky lanterns rise over the city while krathong float down the river — Chiang Mai's most photographed night of the year.

Before you book

A few common questions

How do I book a trip?

Message on LINE or WhatsApp, or fill in the "Plan your trip" form below. Share your dates and group size, and your driver will confirm the details directly with you.

How do I pay?

Pay your driver directly on the day — cash or bank transfer. No online prepayment needed.

Can I change or cancel plans?

Trips can be rescheduled or adjusted — just message as early as you can, and your driver will help work it out.

Do you do airport pickups?

Yes — share your flight number ahead of time so your driver can track it in case of delays.

Is English really spoken the whole trip?

Yes — throughout the entire trip, not just at pickup and drop-off.

How many people fit per car?

Up to 4 guests comfortably per car, with room for luggage. Larger groups can book two cars.
